name: Nonarella
notes: Cozy fallback trattoria for nights when no one could decide where to eat. Plates of pasta and carafes of house wine that made long conversations stretch late.
highlight: Shared plates, shared stories, and the feeling of having a "regular" place in Rome.

name: Fior di Luna
notes: One of the go-to gelato spots in Trastevere for late-night cones and flavor debates.
highlight: Pistachio and stracciatella eaten on cobblestones while the neighborhood buzzed around us.

name: Essenza
notes: Wine, small plates, and cozy evening conversations that stretched far past when we meant to go home.
highlight: Sharing a bottle of red under warm string lights on a random Tuesday.

name: Osteria del Gallo
notes: Classic Roman osteria energy: small room, handwritten menu, and waiters who pretend not to understand when you try to split dishes.
highlight: A dinner that felt like being squeezed into someone else’s family gathering.

name: Fatamorgana
notes: Gelato with wild flavor combinations that made us feel like we had to try something new every time.
highlight: Sampling flavors with names we couldn’t pronounce and picking favorites anyway.

name: Donkey Punch
notes: Sandwiches and drinks in a spot that always felt a little too cool for us, in the best way.
highlight: A quick bite that almost always turned into a longer night than planned.

name: Da Enzo
notes: Worth-the-wait trattoria where every plate felt like a tiny love letter to Roman food.
highlight: A long dinner that felt like the definition of "we're really in Rome."

name: Santi 40
notes: Casual spot for drinks and snacks when we didn’t want the night to end yet.
highlight: A table that slowly filled with friends, glasses, and inside jokes.
